propositions: Review gate runners cannot distinguish clean execution from failed, cancelled, skipped, budget-shed, or resumed work, causing plan-review failures to become empty successful checkpoints and code review to lose earlier work when later criteria raise.

A new discovery submodule must define immutable input plans and typed per-unit outcomes (success, resumed, skipped, shed, failed, cancelled) independent of the existing verify/decide/coach DECISION kernel.

The executor must own dependency-aware scheduling with deterministic ascending-order shedding by dependency rank then stable unit id, such that the shed set is identical across runs and minimal to fit the budget cap.

A versioned digest-complete checkpoint envelope must cover material, code/ref, effective-policy snapshot, prompt, contract, model/mode, topology, dependencies, and schema version, round-tripping only success and content-identical resumed units.

Stored trace must be normalized diagnostic data (ids, outcomes, reason codes, usage, lineage) excluding raw prompts, ticket bodies, provider responses, and secrets, with no per-unit trace added to review/review-status contracts.

The discovery kernel reuses graphlib.static_order scheduling primitive synchronously without asyncio or retry, so no ADR 0065 trigger fires; the empty-graph path for current independent fan-out gates is tested and the dependency digest remains stable across migrations.
